researcher: claude-opus-5-5, psephos-autopilot weekly run 2026-11-02 (M_research v1 refresh, eve of election)
resolution_source: Official state certifications as aggregated by Associated Press race calls; control counted at the seating of the 120th Congress (2027-01-03)
independence_attestation: No betting odds, prediction-market prices or forecast-aggregator numbers were fetched or consulted for this dossier. Searches blocked polymarket/kalshi/manifold/metaculus/predictit/oddschecker; only polling averages and individual polls were used. This research pass ran before the USMID market refresh in the same run.

base_rate_used.reference_class: Postwar midterms where the out-party needed a single-digit net seat gain and led late generic-ballot polling by 5+ points (1954, 2006, 2018 cleanest analogs)

evidence: RCP generic-ballot average 10/8-10/29: D 51.5 / R 43.1 (D+8.4); RCP analysis 2026-10-29 calls it within half a point of the cycle high
Silver Bulletin generic-ballot average reported by Newsweek ~2026-11-01: D 51.2 / R 42.5 (D+8.7) - slightly below the D+9.1 of 2026-10-23
PollCheck (updated 2026-11-01) D+8.2; PollingSource D+8.4; USPollingData D+7.4 (lower-quality page)
Cluster of averages D+7.4 to D+8.7 vs a redistricting-raised threshold of roughly D+2-3 to D+5
questions.strongest_opposing_case: Recent cycles (2016, 2020, 2024) under-stated Republicans; a 4-5 point polling miss toward R combined with the post-redistricting map bias could bring the effective margin close to the threshold, and the averages drifted down ~0.5 pt in the final week.
questions.reasoning_summary: Base 0.85. Final-week averages hold at ~D+8.4 (marginal drift down from D+9.1), leaving ~4-5 pts of cushion over the threshold, a bit over one sigma of historical generic-ballot error. Unchanged net: 0.90.

key_sources.title: RealClearPolitics: Democrats Poised for Largest Generic Ballot Win Since 2008

base_rate_used.reference_class: Complement of the class above: president's party holding the House against a 5+ point late generic-ballot deficit

evidence: Same generic-ballot evidence as the Democratic-majority question (D+7.4 to D+8.7 across averages, 2026-10-29 to 2026-11-01)
questions.strongest_opposing_case: Map bias after mid-decade redistricting plus a systematic R polling miss could let Republicans hold with a popular-vote loss of 3-4 points.
questions.reasoning_summary: Base 0.15 for the president's party holding against a 5+ point late generic deficit. Final-week averages D+7.4 to D+8.7 leave a 4-5 point cushion over the redistricting threshold; scored as the near-complement of the Dem-majority question (exactly one resolves YES at seating): 1 - 0.90 = 0.10.

base_rate_used.reference_class: Postwar midterms in which the out-party gained 4+ Senate seats (~6-7 of ~20 midterms)

evidence: Dems need net +4 (51 seats; VP is R). Polling averages as of ~2026-11-01 (RCP via Election Central/Forbes): NC Cooper +11 (Likely D), GA Ossoff +8 (Likely D hold), MI El-Sayed +3.5 (hold), OH Brown +2.6, TX Talarico +1.4, AK Peltola +1.2, ME Jackson +1.7, IA Hinson (R) +0.5
On polled leaders alone Dems flip NC, OH, TX, AK, ME = 52 seats; NC is the only flip outside ~3 pts
CNN analysis 2026-10-29: plausible range 49 to 55 Democratic seats; 11 of the last 12 quality Maine polls show no clear leader; 6 of last 9 quality Texas polls no clear leader
Generic ballot ~D+8.4 supports a correlated environment in which close races break together
questions.strongest_opposing_case: Four of the five needed flips (OH, TX, AK, ME) are within 3 points in states that voted for Trump or lean R at baseline; the last three presidential-era cycles under-stated Republicans in exactly these kinds of states, and a uniform 2-3 point R miss takes Dems to 48-49. Iowa leaning R and MI being only +3.5 mean there is also downside on the hold side.
questions.reasoning_summary: Base 0.30. Major upgrade since 2026-10-23: final averages show Dem leads in enough R-held seats for 52 (NC comfortably, four more narrowly), plus holds in GA/MI. Because errors are correlated, P(control) is roughly P(the national error does not move ~2 pts toward R), about 0.55-0.6 before the recent-cycle R-miss discount; apply that discount -> 0.52. Moves from 0.40 to 0.52.
